thread:
incident-bot: :warning: realtime-latency-detector triggered for service=runtime-streaming env=prod window=3m p95=0.74s (thr=0.35s) p99=2.4s

alice_nguyen: oncall alerted, joining triage. Paging now.

samir_gupta: oncall here. pulling up dashboards — p99 spike concentrated in us-east-1 streaming cluster.

mike_ops: checking infra events. deploy-bot: any recent rollouts?

deploy-bot: recent-deploys: none in last 30m. autoscaler logs: scale event at 16:42 UTC for pool=streaming-primary.

natasha_support: Support side: 5 customer reports about "streams stalling then resuming" starting ~16:45. No increase in 5xx.

alice_nguyen: sounds like connection stalls / head-of-line blocking. samir — can you check pod churn and socket metrics?

samir_gupta: quick look: node-stream-12 had pod eviction at 16:43 (kube event: DiskPressure), socket backlog spiked, many client reconnects. KV cache miss rate jumped in the same timeframe.

carmen_lee: if it's cache cold + reconnect storm, mitigation: shift some traffic to a prewarmed pool and reduce reconnect pressure (keepalive tweak).

mike_ops: executing mitigation steps now:
```
# exclude bad node from pool
rcctl pool update streaming-primary --exclude-node node-stream-12 --reason "eviction churn"
# create warm pool
rcctl pool create streaming-warm --size 6 --prewarm=true --image runtime:stable
# route some traffic to warm pool
rcctl route update --service runtime --set-weight streaming-warm=40,streaming-primary=60
```

incident-bot: routing change accepted. warm pool creation queued (ETA ~90s).

alice_nguyen: also bump GRPC keepalive to reduce reconnect storms. Set KEEPALIVE=600s on streaming pods.

mike_ops: keepalive patch applied where possible; rolling config will apply to rest. Prewarm script seeding cache on new warm instances.

samir_gupta: monitoring: p95 dropped 740ms -> 310ms after route shift; p99 dropped 2400ms -> 620ms within ~2m. Improvement visible.

dmitri: collecting metrics: kvcache miss rate pre-mitigation 0.12 (baseline ~0.03) -> post-mitigation miss rate trending down to ~0.04. Pod restart reasons show DiskPressure OOM evictions on node-stream-12.

natasha_support: status updates posted to customers: "Engineering applied mitigations (traffic routing + warm pool + keepalive adjustments) — monitoring. Next update in 20m."

alice_nguyen: summary for the page:
- Scope: streaming endpoints in us-east-1
- Impact: intermittent stream stalls, p99 up to ~2.4s; ~120 concurrent sessions impacted; ~5 customers reported
- Probable cause: autoscaler-triggered pod eviction due to disk pressure -> reconnect spike -> KV cache cold -> tail latency increase
- Mitigations: excluded evicted node, spun up warm pool with prewarm seeding, adjusted GRPC keepalive, rerouted traffic

carmen_lee: leaving mitigations in place for 30-40m. Will gradually shift traffic back if stable.

mike_ops: collecting logs bundle and kube events, pushing to INC-2026-351. Also filing infra ticket for disk pressure on node-stream-12.

samir_gupta: next actions for postmortem:
- correlate autoscaler decisions with node disk metrics and kube eviction logs
- investigate prewarm effectiveness and whether prewarming should be automated for streaming pools
- review disk capacity thresholds and eviction policy for streaming nodes
- add circuit breaker for reconnect storms to limit rejoin rate

incident-bot: incident assigned: samir_gupta, mike_ops, alice_nguyen; severity=SEV2. Channel retained for monitoring 40m.

natasha_support: will keep customers updated and close comms after two stable 10m windows.

alice_nguyen: good job. If p99 crosses 1s again we escalate to full page and consider fallback to short-polling behavior for heavy sessions.

mike_ops: warm pool kept at 40% until 17:20 UTC. logs collected at /tmp/incident-351.

samir_gupta: drafting incident summary and timeline for post-incident review.

alice_nguyen: leaving channel open for 45m. Close page if stable at 17:20. Thanks team."
